claims.text: A structure chart decomposes a problem into sub-tasks as boxes: one box per module, the calling module above the modules it calls, joined by vertical lines, with the parameters drawn on those lines - a hollow circle for data and a filled circle for a flag.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A structure chart states what each module does and what passes between them, so the design can be checked before coding begins - every module has one job, and every parameter has a direction and a kind.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A structure chart derives into pseudocode box by box: each box becomes a module, each line beneath a box becomes a call, and each circle on a line becomes a parameter.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A BYREF parameter is shown as data going both ways on the same line, because the value travels down into the module and the changed value travels back up.

claims.text: A state-transition diagram documents an algorithm as states and transitions: each state is one situation the system can be in, and each transition is the event that moves the system from one state to the next.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A state-transition diagram suits an algorithm whose behaviour depends on its history - what the system does next depends on which state it is in - because the diagram shows the states, the events and the resulting states in one picture.
